transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ___. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ___. Um, I came in because... well, I guess I've started doing things at work that just do not make sense. I'm a bookkeeping clerk, and lately I've been taking all the receipts and just lining them up all across the floor. Which, honestly, the floor in our office is so gross. It's this weird, patchy gray carpet that always smells like old coffee because my manager spills his mug literally every morning. He drinks that really cheap hazelnut stuff, it's awful. 

But yeah, I've been lining the receipts up, or I'll sit there and tap my calculator in sets of nine. Nine is a weird number, you know? My cousin used to wear number nine when he played baseball. He almost made it to the minors before he blew out his knee in a dirt bike accident. He lives in Ohio now. Anyway, I also catch myself just standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I just stay like that until someone comes over and asks if I'm okay. The copier is usually jammed anyway, especially if you try to put the thick cardstock in tray two... wait, what was I saying? Oh, yeah, so I guess those things are why I'm here.
Before you do the hand-raising or the other behaviors, do you feel a build-up of tension or an urge that gets better after you do them?

No, not really. I don't feel tense or like I have to do it to feel better. I just sort of find myself doing it. Like, my hands will just be up. It's almost like when you walk into a room and totally forget why you went in there, you know? That happens to me in our breakroom all the time. 

We have this really old fridge in there—the kind with the freezer on the bottom?—and the rubber seal on the door is completely shot, so it hums really loud. Just this constant buzzing noise. My dad actually used to have an old pickup truck that made a noise exactly like that when you turned the key. It was a '98 Ford, I think. We drove it all the way to Florida when I was a kid, and the AC completely died somewhere in Georgia. Have you ever been to Georgia in the middle of July? It's so humid, you feel like you're breathing water just walking across a gas station parking lot... wait, what did you ask me about? Oh, right, tension. Yeah, no, I don't really feel an urge or anything before I do those things.
When you do these behaviors, do they feel purposeful to you, or do they seem automatic and without a clear goal?

Um, no, they don't really feel purposeful. Like, there's no goal to it. I'm just doing things that don't make sense, like I said before, with the receipts on the floor or the calculator tapping. Or the standing by the copier with my hands up. It's just automatic, I guess. 

Speaking of automatic, my mom got this new automatic coffee maker for her house. You can program it from your phone, which is crazy to me. She loves it because she wakes up super early for her job at the bakery. She’s been working there since I was in high school. I used to go in early with her sometimes and help box up the pastries. The smell of fresh bread at 4 AM is honestly the best thing in the world. They make these incredible cheese danishes... but yeah, no, the stuff at work doesn't have a point. I just find myself doing it until someone interrupts me.
When you do these things at work, are you doing them on purpose to annoy or get a reaction from other people?

No, no, I'm definitely not trying to annoy anyone. I actually really like the people I work with, mostly. Well, except for Brenda in HR, she's always leaving passive-aggressive sticky notes on the microwave. Like, we get it, someone didn't cover their soup, but you don't have to use three exclamation points. My sister does that too when she texts me. She'll be like, "Call me back!!!" and I always think it's an emergency, but then it turns out she just wants to know if I remember the name of this cartoon we used to watch when we were kids. It was the one with the talking dog who solved mysteries, but not Scooby-Doo, it was something else... I can never remember the name. We had it on VHS. Remember VHS tapes? You had to rewind them before you took them back to Blockbuster or they'd charge you a fee. My dad got so mad one time because I forgot to rewind Jurassic Park... but no, I'm not doing it on purpose to get a reaction. I just do it.
Can you stop the behavior if you try?

I mean, I don't really know if I can stop it because I don't usually realize I'm doing it until I'm already doing it. Like, someone will ask if I'm okay when I'm just standing there by the copier with my hands up, or I'll look down and realize I've lined up all the receipts across the floor again. Or the calculator thing, tapping it in sets of nine. It's just... I don't know, it just happens. 

Speaking of nine, did you know cats are supposed to have nine lives? I always thought that was a weird saying. Like, why nine? Why not ten? Ten is a nice, round number. My grandma had this cat named Barnaby, and I swear that cat used up all nine of his lives. He got stuck in a tree, he got chased by a raccoon, he even fell into her swimming pool once. My grandma was so upset, she wouldn't let him outside for a month. She used to knit these tiny little sweaters for him, which he hated. He would just flop over on his side and refuse to move until she took it off. She knitted me a sweater once, too, for Christmas. It was this awful mustard yellow color and it was so itchy I couldn't wear it for more than five minutes... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, stopping it. Yeah, I guess if I catch myself, or if someone points it out, I stop. But I don't really try to stop it beforehand because I don't know it's coming.
Before you do these movements, do you feel a sudden urge or sensation that builds up and then goes away after you do them?

No, there's no urge. It's not like a sneeze or an itch where you feel it coming on. Like I said, I just... I just do it. That's actually why I came in, because I started doing these things at work and school that just don't make sense. Like the receipts on the floor, or the calculator tapping in nines, or just standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I'm okay. There's no feeling before it happens. 

Speaking of sneezes, though, my allergies have been so bad lately. The pollen this year is out of control. My car is completely covered in this yellow dust. I had to take it to the car wash twice last week. I usually go to the one on 5th Street because they have the free vacuums, but their vacuums barely have any suction anymore. I tried to vacuum up some french fries that fell between the seats, and it wouldn't even pick them up. I love french fries, though. Especially the curly ones from Arby's. They have that seasoning on them... I tried to find a recipe online to make that seasoning at home, but it just wasn't the same. You need, like, a specific kind of paprika, I think. But yeah, no weird urges or anything before I do the weird stuff at work.
Do you ever choose to do these behaviors on purpose?

No, I definitely don't do them on purpose. It's not a choice. Like I said, I don't even realize I'm doing it most of the time. It's not like I'm sitting there thinking, "Oh, I should line up all these receipts now." Which reminds me, I really need to organize my own receipts at home. I have this shoebox in my closet that's just overflowing with them. I keep telling myself I'm going to sort them out for taxes, but I never do. My uncle got audited once, and it was a whole nightmare. He had to hire this expensive accountant and spend weeks going through old bank statements. He used to own a hardware store, one of those small local ones that sells everything from nails to birdseed. I used to love going in there when I was a kid because it always smelled like sawdust and motor oil. He had this old golden retriever named Buster who would just sleep under the counter all day. Customers used to bring him treats... but yeah, no, I'm not choosing to do the weird stuff. It just happens.
Have you ever done things like this on purpose to break rules or deliberately annoy people?

No, never. I'm not trying to cause trouble or annoy anyone. I actually hate when people are annoyed with me, it makes my stomach hurt. Like this one time in high school, I accidentally knocked over my friend's science project—it was this volcano thing made of papier-mâché—and she was so mad at me. She wouldn't talk to me for a whole week. I tried to make it up to her by buying her a coffee from Starbucks, but I got her order wrong. She wanted a caramel macchiato with oat milk, and I got her regular milk. I didn't know people could be so picky about milk. I mean, milk is just milk, right? Although I did try almond milk once and it tasted like dusty water. I don't get the hype. My mom buys it all the time now because she says it's better for her digestion. She's been on this whole health kick lately, buying all these organic vegetables and weird seeds... chia seeds, I think? They get stuck in your teeth. But no, I definitely don't do any of this stuff to break rules or bother people. It's embarrassing, really.
Do you feel like you have to do these behaviors to prevent something bad from happening?

No, not at all. It's not about preventing anything bad. I don't think like, oh, if I don't tap the nines on the calculator, my house is going to burn down or something. It's nothing like that. 

But speaking of bad things happening, my cousin just got into a really bad fender bender last week. He was driving down Route 9, right by where that old indoor mall used to be? They're tearing it down now to build luxury apartments, which I think is a terrible idea because the traffic there is already a total nightmare. Anyway, this guy just completely rear-ended him out of nowhere. Smashed the whole trunk of his Honda in. And it really sucks because he literally just bought brand new tires for it the day before. Tires are so expensive now, it's ridiculous. And the guys at the shop always try to upsell you on those road hazard warranties. I never buy the warranty for anything. Like when I bought my TV, the cashier would not stop pushing the three-year protection plan on me. I just wanted to pay and leave, you know? But yeah, no, I don't do any of those weird behaviors to stop bad things from happening. It just happens.
If you try to hold back the behavior once it starts, can you suppress it for a short while?

I mean, I guess I can hold it back for a minute if I really try, but it's hard. Like, if I'm at work and I start lining up the receipts across the floor, and my boss walks by, I can stop for a second. But it's just... I don't know why I'm even doing it. It doesn't make sense. Like standing by the copier with my hands up in the air until someone asks if I'm okay... I can put my hands down if I really focus, but then I just feel weird. 

Speaking of the copier, our office just got a new one and it is incredibly confusing. It has this huge touchscreen menu that looks like an iPad, but none of the buttons do what you think they're going to do. I tried to scan a double-sided document yesterday and it ended up emailing it to the entire accounting department. Which was so embarrassing because it was just a lunch menu for that new Thai place down the street. Have you tried Thai food? I love Pad Thai, but only if they don't put too many peanuts on it. Some places just drown it in peanuts and then that's all you can taste. My friend Sarah is actually deathly allergic to peanuts. Like, she has to carry an EpiPen everywhere she goes. We went to a baseball game once and she couldn't even sit in our section because people were eating peanuts a few rows down. It must be so stressful to live like that, always worrying about what's in your food. But anyway, yeah, I can suppress the weird stuff for a little bit, like the calculator tapping... I tap it in sets of nine... but it always comes back.
When you do these behaviors, are they usually the same exact movement or pattern each time?

I'm not really sure if it's the exact same movement every time. I mean, I don't really pay that close attention to it. Like with the receipts, I just line them up, but I don't know if I use my left hand first or if I space them exactly the same way. It's not like a choreographed dance or anything. 

Speaking of dances, my sister is a dance teacher, and she's trying to put together this recital for her little kids, the five-year-olds. She's been complaining non-stop because they just run around the studio and won't stand on their little tape marks. She uses this bright pink gaffer tape on the floor so they know where to stand. Gaffer tape is actually super strong, it's way better than duct tape. I used some to fix the bumper on my car after that time I backed into a light pole at the grocery store. It was raining so hard I couldn't see out the back window, and the backup camera was all blurry. Those cameras are useless in the rain anyway. But yeah, the tape held the bumper on for like six months before I finally got it fixed. The auto body guy laughed at me, but it saved me from having to pay my deductible right away. Deductibles are such a scam anyway, you pay for insurance every month and then you still have to pay when something happens? It makes no sense. But I don't know about the patterns, honestly. I don't think it's exactly the same every single time.
Do you ever make sudden movements or sounds that you can’t really control, like blinking, shoulder jerks, sniffing, or throat clearing?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I don't have sudden jerks or make sounds I can't control. I mean, sometimes my throat gets dry, but I don't clear it constantly or anything. 

Speaking of dry throats, the air conditioning in my office is always blasting. It's like an icebox in there, especially in the summer. Everyone brings space heaters to keep under their desks, which I'm pretty sure is a huge fire hazard. The building manager, this guy named Gary, he sends out these passive-aggressive emails every month about how space heaters are strictly prohibited, but no one listens to him. Gary is actually kind of a weird guy. He collects antique doorknobs. He showed me pictures of them once on his phone. He has like, hundreds of them mounted on these velvet boards in his basement. It's such a specific thing to collect, you know? My grandfather used to collect coins, which makes a lot more sense. He had this one silver dollar from the 1800s that he kept in a little plastic case. He said it was worth a lot of money, but when we tried to sell it after he passed away, the coin shop guy said it was a fake. Can you believe that? My poor grandpa probably got scammed at a flea market or something. People will fake anything these days. I saw a documentary about people faking vintage wine, printing out labels on their home computers and putting cheap wine in old bottles. It's crazy what people will do for money. But yeah, no, I don't have any sudden movements or blinking or anything like that.
When you do these behaviors, is it the same exact movement or routine each time?

I mean, I guess it is kind of the same routine. Like I was saying, I came in because I've just started doing these things at work—and at school, too—that just don't make any sense. Like lining the receipts across the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine. Always nine. Or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I'm okay. 

It's so weird, right? Like, why would I do that? But speaking of school, I'm taking this accounting class at the community college right now, and the professor is just... he's so monotone. He sounds exactly like that guy from those old dry eye commercials, you know? Like, "Bueller... Bueller..." It's impossible to stay awake. And the seats in the lecture hall are those terrible plastic ones that are attached to the desk, so you can't even adjust them. My back always kills me after an hour. I actually tried bringing a little lumbar pillow last week, but I left it on the bus on the way home. The public transit in this city is a nightmare anyway. The buses are never on time. I waited 45 minutes in the freezing cold on Tuesday because two buses just drove right past me without stopping. They put up this new digital sign at the bus stop that's supposed to tell you when the next one is coming, but it just said "Error 404" the whole time. Like, how does a bus stop get a web error? It's ridiculous. But yeah, the behaviors... they are pretty much the same routines, like the sets of nine and the receipts.
When you do these behaviors, do they feel like repeated movements or routines that you just get stuck doing?

I don't really know if I'd say I get stuck doing them. I mean, I guess I do it until it's done, right? Like the tapping, I just do the nine taps and then I stop. It's not like I'm trapped there forever. 

Speaking of being trapped, did you know that in some older elevators, if the power goes out, the emergency brakes clamp down so hard you can actually feel the whole car shudder? I read this article about elevator mechanics the other day because my building's elevator has been making this awful grinding noise. It sounds like two pieces of sheet metal rubbing together. The maintenance guy, Steve—he’s the one who replaced Gary after the whole space heater incident—he says it's just the cables stretching because it's getting colder outside. Which doesn't even make sense because the elevator shaft is inside the building. Steve is always making excuses like that. Last month he said the water pressure was low because of a "solar flare." A solar flare! I mean, I'm just a bookkeeper, I don't know much about plumbing, but I'm pretty sure the sun doesn't affect the pipes in a three-story apartment building. I actually started keeping a log of all the weird excuses Steve gives. I have it in a spreadsheet on my laptop. I use Excel for everything now. I even made a spreadsheet to track my grocery spending, but then the grocery store changed their layout and moved the cereal aisle, which completely ruined my system. I hate when they do that. You go in looking for Cheerios and end up in the pet food section. But yeah, no, I don't feel like I'm stuck doing the routines, I just do them and then move on to whatever else I'm supposed to be doing.
When you try to hold back these behaviors, can you suppress them for more than a few seconds or minutes?

I mean, I don't really know. I've never actually tried to hold them back, so I couldn't tell you if I can suppress them or not. I just do them. 

Why would I try to stop, you know? It's just part of my day. Kind of like how I always get my coffee from this one specific cart outside my office building. The guy who runs it, his name is Sal, he knows exactly how I like it—medium roast, splash of oat milk, no sugar. Sal's great. He used to be a jazz musician, actually. He plays the saxophone. He told me he used to tour all over Europe in the nineties. He said the coffee in Italy completely changed his life, which is why he started the cart. He has all these crazy stories about playing in these tiny, smoky underground clubs in Paris and Berlin. It sounds so glamorous, right? Way more glamorous than bookkeeping, that's for sure. I tried to learn an instrument once, back in high school. I picked the trumpet because I thought it looked cool, but my lips would just get so sore, and my mom said I sounded like a dying goose. So that didn't last long. I still have the trumpet, though. It's sitting in its case in the back of my closet, probably gathering dust. I should probably sell it or donate it to a school band or something. Instruments are so expensive, and there's probably some kid out there who really wants to learn how to play but can't afford one. But anyway, yeah, I've never really tried to hold back the tapping or the receipts, so I'm not sure how long I could stop it for if I tried.
When you do these behaviors, do you feel aware of yourself doing them, or do they seem to happen outside your control?

I mean, I'm definitely aware I'm doing them. It's not like I'm blacking out or someone else is controlling my body. I know I'm standing there with my hands up by the copier, or tapping the calculator nine times, or putting the receipts all over the floor. I know I'm doing it. It's just... I don't know why I'm doing it. Like, it doesn't make any sense. 

Which is really frustrating because usually everything I do makes sense. I'm a bookkeeper, you know? Everything has to balance. Every penny has to be accounted for. My boss, Mr. Henderson, he's a stickler for the details. He's this older guy, always wears these terrible sweater vests. Like, argyle sweater vests in the middle of July. I don't know how he doesn't sweat to death in the office, especially because the AC in our building is basically a suggestion. The vents just kind of rattle and blow out lukewarm air. It smells a little bit like old wet paper, too. I brought it up to Steve—the maintenance guy I told you about—and he said the smell was from the "humidity inversion" in the ductwork. Again with the made-up science! I swear he just strings words together to see if I'll believe him. I actually looked up humidity inversion on my phone while he was talking, and it's a real meteorological thing, but it happens in the atmosphere, not in the ceiling of a strip mall accounting firm. I should add that to my spreadsheet. "Steve claims weather phenomenon happening inside office." It's just wild. But yeah, I'm aware I'm doing the things with the receipts and the copier, they just don't make sense to do.
Do you ever do these behaviors just to break rules or show defiance?

No, no, it's not about breaking rules at all. I'm actually a really rule-abiding guy. Like I said, I'm a bookkeeper, so rules are kind of my whole life. The IRS has so many rules, and if you mess them up, the fines are crazy. But no, I don't do the things to be defiant. Like I told you when I first came in, I'm only here because I started doing all these things at work and school that just don't make any sense. The lining the receipts up across the floor, the tapping the calculator in sets of nine, standing by the copier with my hands up in the air until someone asks if I'm okay... I don't want to do them, and I'm definitely not trying to get in trouble. 

Getting in trouble at work is the worst, especially with Mr. Henderson. He gets this little vein that pops out on his forehead when he's mad. It's right above his left eyebrow, and it pulses. It's honestly a little distracting. One time, this guy David—he used to work in payroll—he accidentally shredded a whole stack of original W-2s instead of the copies. Mr. Henderson's vein was practically vibrating. David tried to tape them back together, which is just insane. You can't tape a shredded W-2 and send it to the government. They use those cross-cut shredders now, so it was basically confetti. David actually got fired over that. Now he works at a car dealership, I think. Selling used Hondas or something. Hondas are pretty reliable cars, though. My aunt had a Civic that lasted for like, three hundred thousand miles. The only reason it died was because she drove it into a flooded intersection during a storm. The water came right up over the hood. The fire department had to come get her out in a raft. She was so mad about her groceries in the trunk getting ruined. But yeah, no, I'm not trying to be defiant or break rules. I just do these weird things and I don't know why.
Do you ever perform the same repetitive movement over and over for several seconds or minutes, like rocking, hand-flapping, or body posturing?

I mean, yeah, I guess so. Like I was saying before, that's the whole reason I'm here. I started doing all these weird things at work and school that just don't make any sense at all. Like standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air. I just stand there like that until someone comes by and asks if I'm okay. Or the calculator thing, where I have to tap it in sets of nine. And the receipts, lining them all up across the floor... 

It's so annoying with the receipts because thermal paper fades so fast, you know? If you leave a receipt in your car on a hot day, it just turns completely black. Or if it's in your wallet too long, the ink just disappears and it's a blank piece of paper. I don't understand why they still use thermal printers. It seems like a terrible way to keep permanent records. My dad used to keep all his receipts in this old shoebox under his bed for taxes. It was a Nike box, from these running shoes he bought when he decided he was going to run a marathon. He never actually ran the marathon, though. He trained for like three weeks, pulled a hamstring, and gave up. He said running was bad for your knees anyway. He started swimming instead. He goes to the YMCA every morning at 5 AM. I don't know how anyone wakes up that early on purpose. The pool always smells so strongly of chlorine, it burns my eyes just walking into the building. But yeah, I do those things like the copier and the tapping and the receipts over and over, even though they don't make sense.
When you do these repetitive behaviors, are they usually done to break rules or show defiance?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like I was saying a few minutes ago, no, it's not about breaking rules or being defiant at all. I actually hate breaking rules. Even really small ones, like jaywalking. I'll stand at a crosswalk at midnight when there are absolutely zero cars on the road, just waiting for the little white walking guy to light up. 

My friend Tyler used to make fun of me for it all the time. He was always breaking rules, though. Back in high school, he actually got suspended for climbing up onto the roof of the gym just to get a frisbee. Which is so stupid when you think about it, because frisbees are like, what, maybe five dollars? You can literally get them at the dollar store now. They have that whole aisle of cheap plastic summer toys. I bought a squirt gun there once for my little cousin, and it leaked the second I put water in it. Just dripped straight out the bottom of the handle right onto my shoes. I guess you really get what you pay for with that kind of stuff. The plastic is probably terrible for the environment, too. But yeah, to answer your question again, I'm definitely not trying to be defiant or break any rules when I do the weird stuff at work.
Do you feel like you choose to do these behaviors, even a little bit?

No, not at all. That's the whole problem, honestly. Like I said, I only came in here because I started doing all these things at work and school that just don't make any sense, and I don't feel like I'm choosing to do them. The lining the receipts up across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I'm okay... I don't want to do any of it. 

It's actually really embarrassing, especially the copier thing. The copier is right next to the breakroom, so everyone walks past it when they go to get coffee. We just got one of those fancy Keurig machines, too. The ones where you can pick the exact ounce size for your cup. It's supposed to be a perk, but honestly, those little plastic pods are so bad for the earth. I saw a documentary once about how many of those K-cups end up in landfills, and it's millions. They just sit there for centuries because the plastic doesn't break down. It made me want to start composting, but I live in an apartment on the third floor, so I don't really have a yard for a compost bin. My neighbor has a little worm bin on her balcony, though. She says they eat all her vegetable scraps. I think worms are kind of gross, to be honest. They get all slimy when it rains. But yeah, I don't choose to do the weird behaviors. They just happen.

patient.answer:
Hi, Dr. ___. Um, I came in because... well, I guess I've started doing things at work that just do not make sense. I'm a bookkeeping clerk, and lately I've been taking all the receipts and just lining them up all across the floor. Which, honestly, the floor in our office is so gross. It's this weird, patchy gray carpet that always smells like old coffee because my manager spills his mug literally every morning. He drinks that really cheap hazelnut stuff, it's awful. 

But yeah, I've been lining the receipts up, or I'll sit there and tap my calculator in sets of nine. Nine is a weird number, you know? My cousin used to wear number nine when he played baseball. He almost made it to the minors before he blew out his knee in a dirt bike accident. He lives in Ohio now. Anyway, I also catch myself just standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air, and I just stay like that until someone comes over and asks if I'm okay. The copier is usually jammed anyway, especially if you try to put the thick cardstock in tray two... wait, what was I saying? Oh, yeah, so I guess those things are why I'm here.

inference.note: Added obsessive-compulsive disorder with mixed obsessional thoughts and acts due to repetitive, ritualized behaviors; stereotypic movement disorder and unspecified conduct disorder remain less likely differentials.

doctor.intent: To distinguish a compulsive ritual from a motor tic/stereotypy by checking whether the behavior is preceded by a strong urge or tension that is relieved by doing it.
doctor.question: Before you do the hand-raising or the other behaviors, do you feel a build-up of tension or an urge that gets better after you do them?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a build-up of tension or an urge preceding the behaviors, which is a screening question for compulsions (as in OCD). My symptom profile does not include compulsions or tension/urges related to these behaviors.

patient.answer:
No, not really. I don't feel tense or like I have to do it to feel better. I just sort of find myself doing it. Like, my hands will just be up. It's almost like when you walk into a room and totally forget why you went in there, you know? That happens to me in our breakroom all the time. 

We have this really old fridge in there—the kind with the freezer on the bottom?—and the rubber seal on the door is completely shot, so it hums really loud. Just this constant buzzing noise. My dad actually used to have an old pickup truck that made a noise exactly like that when you turned the key. It was a '98 Ford, I think. We drove it all the way to Florida when I was a kid, and the AC completely died somewhere in Georgia. Have you ever been to Georgia in the middle of July? It's so humid, you feel like you're breathing water just walking across a gas station parking lot... wait, what did you ask me about? Oh, right, tension. Yeah, no, I don't really feel an urge or anything before I do those things.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the repetitive behaviors are purposeful/organized versus purposeless/involuntary, which helps distinguish stereotypic movement disorder from a conduct-related pattern.
doctor.question: When you do these behaviors, do they feel purposeful to you, or do they seem automatic and without a clear goal?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature of the disorganized behaviors (lining up receipts, tapping the calculator, standing with hands up) to determine if they are purposeful or automatic, which directly relates to the symptom of disorganized/abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
Um, no, they don't really feel purposeful. Like, there's no goal to it. I'm just doing things that don't make sense, like I said before, with the receipts on the floor or the calculator tapping. Or the standing by the copier with my hands up. It's just automatic, I guess. 

Speaking of automatic, my mom got this new automatic coffee maker for her house. You can program it from your phone, which is crazy to me. She loves it because she wakes up super early for her job at the bakery. She’s been working there since I was in high school. I used to go in early with her sometimes and help box up the pastries. The smell of fresh bread at 4 AM is honestly the best thing in the world. They make these incredible cheese danishes... but yeah, no, the stuff at work doesn't have a point. I just find myself doing it until someone interrupts me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behaviors are deliberately provocative/oppositional versus involuntary repetitive actions, to distinguish a conduct-related disorder from a stereotypic movement disorder
doctor.question: When you do these things at work, are you doing them on purpose to annoy or get a reaction from other people?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the disorganized behaviors are done intentionally to annoy others or get a reaction, which is a follow-up to clarify the nature of my chief complaint (S022). It does not match any new symptom in my profile.

patient.answer: No, no, I'm definitely not trying to annoy anyone. I actually really like the people I work with, mostly. Well, except for Brenda in HR, she's always leaving passive-aggressive sticky notes on the microwave. Like, we get it, someone didn't cover their soup, but you don't have to use three exclamation points. My sister does that too when she texts me. She'll be like, "Call me back!!!" and I always think it's an emergency, but then it turns out she just wants to know if I remember the name of this cartoon we used to watch when we were kids. It was the one with the talking dog who solved mysteries, but not Scooby-Doo, it was something else... I can never remember the name. We had it on VHS. Remember VHS tapes? You had to rewind them before you took them back to Blockbuster or they'd charge you a fee. My dad got so mad one time because I forgot to rewind Jurassic Park... but no, I'm not doing it on purpose to get a reaction. I just do it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the repetitive behaviors are at least partly under voluntary control, which would favor a conduct/problem-behavior diagnosis over an involuntary tic/stereotypy picture.
doctor.question: Can you stop the behavior if you try?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is continuing to ask about the abnormal behaviors (like standing by the copier with hands up) to determine if I have voluntary control over them, which relates to disorganized or abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
I mean, I don't really know if I can stop it because I don't usually realize I'm doing it until I'm already doing it. Like, someone will ask if I'm okay when I'm just standing there by the copier with my hands up, or I'll look down and realize I've lined up all the receipts across the floor again. Or the calculator thing, tapping it in sets of nine. It's just... I don't know, it just happens. 

Speaking of nine, did you know cats are supposed to have nine lives? I always thought that was a weird saying. Like, why nine? Why not ten? Ten is a nice, round number. My grandma had this cat named Barnaby, and I swear that cat used up all nine of his lives. He got stuck in a tree, he got chased by a raccoon, he even fell into her swimming pool once. My grandma was so upset, she wouldn't let him outside for a month. She used to knit these tiny little sweaters for him, which he hated. He would just flop over on his side and refuse to move until she took it off. She knitted me a sweater once, too, for Christmas. It was this awful mustard yellow color and it was so itchy I couldn't wear it for more than five minutes... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, stopping it. Yeah, I guess if I catch myself, or if someone points it out, I stop. But I don't really try to stop it beforehand because I don't know it's coming.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a tic-like, semi-involuntary behavior from a conduct/behavioral disturbance by assessing whether the movements are preceded by a sudden, irresistible urge or sensation (premonitory urge).
doctor.question: Before you do these movements, do you feel a sudden urge or sensation that builds up and then goes away after you do them?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the internal experience preceding the abnormal movements to determine if they are tics, compulsions, or disorganized behavior, which relates directly to my symptom of Disorganized Abnormal Behavior.

patient.answer:
No, there's no urge. It's not like a sneeze or an itch where you feel it coming on. Like I said, I just... I just do it. That's actually why I came in, because I started doing these things at work and school that just don't make sense. Like the receipts on the floor, or the calculator tapping in nines, or just standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I'm okay. There's no feeling before it happens. 

Speaking of sneezes, though, my allergies have been so bad lately. The pollen this year is out of control. My car is completely covered in this yellow dust. I had to take it to the car wash twice last week. I usually go to the one on 5th Street because they have the free vacuums, but their vacuums barely have any suction anymore. I tried to vacuum up some french fries that fell between the seats, and it wouldn't even pick them up. I love french fries, though. Especially the curly ones from Arby's. They have that seasoning on them... I tried to find a recipe online to make that seasoning at home, but it just wasn't the same. You need, like, a specific kind of paprika, I think. But yeah, no weird urges or anything before I do the weird stuff at work.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behavior is intentional and goal-directed versus automatic/involuntary, to separate tic disorder from oppositional/conduct-related behavior
doctor.question: Do you ever choose to do these behaviors on purpose?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient chooses to do the disorganized behaviors on purpose (volitional vs. non-volitional). The patient already discussed S022 (Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior) and clarified in previous turns that they don't do it on purpose, but the doctor is reiterating/asking about intentionality again. There is no specific symptom profile item for 'choosing behaviors on purpose' other than the already manifested S022, which doesn't explicitly state whether it's on purpose or not in the manifestation, but the patient has already addressed S022.

patient.answer: No, I definitely don't do them on purpose. It's not a choice. Like I said, I don't even realize I'm doing it most of the time. It's not like I'm sitting there thinking, "Oh, I should line up all these receipts now." Which reminds me, I really need to organize my own receipts at home. I have this shoebox in my closet that's just overflowing with them. I keep telling myself I'm going to sort them out for taxes, but I never do. My uncle got audited once, and it was a whole nightmare. He had to hire this expensive accountant and spend weeks going through old bank statements. He used to own a hardware store, one of those small local ones that sells everything from nails to birdseed. I used to love going in there when I was a kid because it always smelled like sawdust and motor oil. He had this old golden retriever named Buster who would just sleep under the counter all day. Customers used to bring him treats... but yeah, no, I'm not choosing to do the weird stuff. It just happens.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behavior is a voluntary, purposeful pattern of violating rules or rights, which would support a conduct-type diagnosis rather than an involuntary stereotypic behavior
doctor.question: Have you ever done things like this on purpose to break rules or deliberately annoy people?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the behaviors are done intentionally to break rules or annoy others, which would suggest Oppositional Defiant Disorder or Antisocial traits. My profile does not contain any symptoms related to intentional rule-breaking or defiant behavior.

patient.answer: No, never. I'm not trying to cause trouble or annoy anyone. I actually hate when people are annoyed with me, it makes my stomach hurt. Like this one time in high school, I accidentally knocked over my friend's science project—it was this volcano thing made of papier-mâché—and she was so mad at me. She wouldn't talk to me for a whole week. I tried to make it up to her by buying her a coffee from Starbucks, but I got her order wrong. She wanted a caramel macchiato with oat milk, and I got her regular milk. I didn't know people could be so picky about milk. I mean, milk is just milk, right? Although I did try almond milk once and it tasted like dusty water. I don't get the hype. My mom buys it all the time now because she says it's better for her digestion. She's been on this whole health kick lately, buying all these organic vegetables and weird seeds... chia seeds, I think? They get stuck in your teeth. But no, I definitely don't do any of this stuff to break rules or bother people. It's embarrassing, really.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behavior is to prevent harm or reduce distress from an obsession, which would support a compulsive disorder rather than a stereotypic/repetitive behavior disorder
doctor.question: Do you feel like you have to do these behaviors to prevent something bad from happening?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the behaviors are compulsions performed to prevent something bad from happening (a symptom of OCD). My symptom profile does not include compulsions or OCD symptoms; my behaviors are disorganized/abnormal (S022) but not driven by a need to prevent a negative outcome.

patient.answer:
No, not at all. It's not about preventing anything bad. I don't think like, oh, if I don't tap the nines on the calculator, my house is going to burn down or something. It's nothing like that. 

But speaking of bad things happening, my cousin just got into a really bad fender bender last week. He was driving down Route 9, right by where that old indoor mall used to be? They're tearing it down now to build luxury apartments, which I think is a terrible idea because the traffic there is already a total nightmare. Anyway, this guy just completely rear-ended him out of nowhere. Smashed the whole trunk of his Honda in. And it really sucks because he literally just bought brand new tires for it the day before. Tires are so expensive now, it's ridiculous. And the guys at the shop always try to upsell you on those road hazard warranties. I never buy the warranty for anything. Like when I bought my TV, the cashier would not stop pushing the three-year protection plan on me. I just wanted to pay and leave, you know? But yeah, no, I don't do any of those weird behaviors to stop bad things from happening. It just happens.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a complex tic/other involuntary stereotyped movement from a habitual or ritualized behavior by checking for suppressibility
doctor.question: If you try to hold back the behavior once it starts, can you suppress it for a short while?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I can suppress the unusual behaviors, which relates to my symptoms of disorganized or abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
I mean, I guess I can hold it back for a minute if I really try, but it's hard. Like, if I'm at work and I start lining up the receipts across the floor, and my boss walks by, I can stop for a second. But it's just... I don't know why I'm even doing it. It doesn't make sense. Like standing by the copier with my hands up in the air until someone asks if I'm okay... I can put my hands down if I really focus, but then I just feel weird. 

Speaking of the copier, our office just got a new one and it is incredibly confusing. It has this huge touchscreen menu that looks like an iPad, but none of the buttons do what you think they're going to do. I tried to scan a double-sided document yesterday and it ended up emailing it to the entire accounting department. Which was so embarrassing because it was just a lunch menu for that new Thai place down the street. Have you tried Thai food? I love Pad Thai, but only if they don't put too many peanuts on it. Some places just drown it in peanuts and then that's all you can taste. My friend Sarah is actually deathly allergic to peanuts. Like, she has to carry an EpiPen everywhere she goes. We went to a baseball game once and she couldn't even sit in our section because people were eating peanuts a few rows down. It must be so stressful to live like that, always worrying about what's in your food. But anyway, yeah, I can suppress the weird stuff for a little bit, like the calculator tapping... I tap it in sets of nine... but it always comes back.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behaviors are repetitive, stereotyped movements typical of a tic/stereotypy rather than deliberate oppositional behavior
doctor.question: When you do these behaviors, are they usually the same exact movement or pattern each time?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the behaviors are stereotyped (the exact same movement or pattern each time) to rule out stereotypic movement disorder or motor tics, which is not covered by the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I'm not really sure if it's the exact same movement every time. I mean, I don't really pay that close attention to it. Like with the receipts, I just line them up, but I don't know if I use my left hand first or if I space them exactly the same way. It's not like a choreographed dance or anything. 

Speaking of dances, my sister is a dance teacher, and she's trying to put together this recital for her little kids, the five-year-olds. She's been complaining non-stop because they just run around the studio and won't stand on their little tape marks. She uses this bright pink gaffer tape on the floor so they know where to stand. Gaffer tape is actually super strong, it's way better than duct tape. I used some to fix the bumper on my car after that time I backed into a light pole at the grocery store. It was raining so hard I couldn't see out the back window, and the backup camera was all blurry. Those cameras are useless in the rain anyway. But yeah, the tape held the bumper on for like six months before I finally got it fixed. The auto body guy laughed at me, but it saved me from having to pay my deductible right away. Deductibles are such a scam anyway, you pay for insurance every month and then you still have to pay when something happens? It makes no sense. But I don't know about the patterns, honestly. I don't think it's exactly the same every single time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the repetitive behaviors are sudden, rapid, and involuntary motor/vocal tics versus purposeful/oppositional behavior
doctor.question: Do you ever make sudden movements or sounds that you can’t really control, like blinking, shoulder jerks, sniffing, or throat clearing?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about motor or vocal tics (e.g., blinking, shoulder jerks, sniffing, throat clearing), which are not covered by any of my symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
No, I don't really do anything like that. I don't have sudden jerks or make sounds I can't control. I mean, sometimes my throat gets dry, but I don't clear it constantly or anything. 

Speaking of dry throats, the air conditioning in my office is always blasting. It's like an icebox in there, especially in the summer. Everyone brings space heaters to keep under their desks, which I'm pretty sure is a huge fire hazard. The building manager, this guy named Gary, he sends out these passive-aggressive emails every month about how space heaters are strictly prohibited, but no one listens to him. Gary is actually kind of a weird guy. He collects antique doorknobs. He showed me pictures of them once on his phone. He has like, hundreds of them mounted on these velvet boards in his basement. It's such a specific thing to collect, you know? My grandfather used to collect coins, which makes a lot more sense. He had this one silver dollar from the 1800s that he kept in a little plastic case. He said it was worth a lot of money, but when we tried to sell it after he passed away, the coin shop guy said it was a fake. Can you believe that? My poor grandpa probably got scammed at a flea market or something. People will fake anything these days. I saw a documentary about people faking vintage wine, printing out labels on their home computers and putting cheap wine in old bottles. It's crazy what people will do for money. But yeah, no, I don't have any sudden movements or blinking or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a tic-like/automatic repetitive movement from a volitional behavior disorder by assessing whether the behavior is stereotyped and repetitive in the same way each time
doctor.question: When you do these behaviors, is it the same exact movement or routine each time?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for more details about the abnormal behaviors I mentioned earlier, specifically whether they are repetitive or stereotyped routines, which falls under disorganized and abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
I mean, I guess it is kind of the same routine. Like I was saying, I came in because I've just started doing these things at work—and at school, too—that just don't make any sense. Like lining the receipts across the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine. Always nine. Or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I'm okay. 

It's so weird, right? Like, why would I do that? But speaking of school, I'm taking this accounting class at the community college right now, and the professor is just... he's so monotone. He sounds exactly like that guy from those old dry eye commercials, you know? Like, "Bueller... Bueller..." It's impossible to stay awake. And the seats in the lecture hall are those terrible plastic ones that are attached to the desk, so you can't even adjust them. My back always kills me after an hour. I actually tried bringing a little lumbar pillow last week, but I left it on the bus on the way home. The public transit in this city is a nightmare anyway. The buses are never on time. I waited 45 minutes in the freezing cold on Tuesday because two buses just drove right past me without stopping. They put up this new digital sign at the bus stop that's supposed to tell you when the next one is coming, but it just said "Error 404" the whole time. Like, how does a bus stop get a web error? It's ridiculous. But yeah, the behaviors... they are pretty much the same routines, like the sets of nine and the receipts.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the repetitive behaviors are stereotyped motor movements/complex mannerisms versus oppositional, hostile, or rule-breaking behavior
doctor.question: When you do these behaviors, do they feel like repeated movements or routines that you just get stuck doing?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the behaviors feel like compulsions (routines you get stuck doing), which is a symptom of OCD or related disorders. This is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I don't really know if I'd say I get stuck doing them. I mean, I guess I do it until it's done, right? Like the tapping, I just do the nine taps and then I stop. It's not like I'm trapped there forever. 

Speaking of being trapped, did you know that in some older elevators, if the power goes out, the emergency brakes clamp down so hard you can actually feel the whole car shudder? I read this article about elevator mechanics the other day because my building's elevator has been making this awful grinding noise. It sounds like two pieces of sheet metal rubbing together. The maintenance guy, Steve—he’s the one who replaced Gary after the whole space heater incident—he says it's just the cables stretching because it's getting colder outside. Which doesn't even make sense because the elevator shaft is inside the building. Steve is always making excuses like that. Last month he said the water pressure was low because of a "solar flare." A solar flare! I mean, I'm just a bookkeeper, I don't know much about plumbing, but I'm pretty sure the sun doesn't affect the pipes in a three-story apartment building. I actually started keeping a log of all the weird excuses Steve gives. I have it in a spreadsheet on my laptop. I use Excel for everything now. I even made a spreadsheet to track my grocery spending, but then the grocery store changed their layout and moved the cereal aisle, which completely ruined my system. I hate when they do that. You go in looking for Cheerios and end up in the pet food section. But yeah, no, I don't feel like I'm stuck doing the routines, I just do them and then move on to whatever else I'm supposed to be doing.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a tic disorder from a stereotypic movement disorder by assessing whether the behavior is suppressible for longer than a brief moment with rising discomfort.
doctor.question: When you try to hold back these behaviors, can you suppress them for more than a few seconds or minutes?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the behaviors can be temporarily suppressed, which is a characteristic of tics. The patient's symptom profile does not include information about the suppressibility of these behaviors.

patient.answer:
I mean, I don't really know. I've never actually tried to hold them back, so I couldn't tell you if I can suppress them or not. I just do them. 

Why would I try to stop, you know? It's just part of my day. Kind of like how I always get my coffee from this one specific cart outside my office building. The guy who runs it, his name is Sal, he knows exactly how I like it—medium roast, splash of oat milk, no sugar. Sal's great. He used to be a jazz musician, actually. He plays the saxophone. He told me he used to tour all over Europe in the nineties. He said the coffee in Italy completely changed his life, which is why he started the cart. He has all these crazy stories about playing in these tiny, smoky underground clubs in Paris and Berlin. It sounds so glamorous, right? Way more glamorous than bookkeeping, that's for sure. I tried to learn an instrument once, back in high school. I picked the trumpet because I thought it looked cool, but my lips would just get so sore, and my mom said I sounded like a dying goose. So that didn't last long. I still have the trumpet, though. It's sitting in its case in the back of my closet, probably gathering dust. I should probably sell it or donate it to a school band or something. Instruments are so expensive, and there's probably some kid out there who really wants to learn how to play but can't afford one. But anyway, yeah, I've never really tried to hold back the tapping or the receipts, so I'm not sure how long I could stop it for if I tried.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behavior is voluntary and mischievous vs involuntary/automatic, to distinguish conduct disorder/other disruptive behavior from stereotyped movement disorder
doctor.question: When you do these behaviors, do you feel aware of yourself doing them, or do they seem to happen outside your control?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's level of awareness and control regarding the disorganized and abnormal behaviors they have been discussing (tapping, lining up receipts, standing by the copier).

patient.answer:
I mean, I'm definitely aware I'm doing them. It's not like I'm blacking out or someone else is controlling my body. I know I'm standing there with my hands up by the copier, or tapping the calculator nine times, or putting the receipts all over the floor. I know I'm doing it. It's just... I don't know why I'm doing it. Like, it doesn't make any sense. 

Which is really frustrating because usually everything I do makes sense. I'm a bookkeeper, you know? Everything has to balance. Every penny has to be accounted for. My boss, Mr. Henderson, he's a stickler for the details. He's this older guy, always wears these terrible sweater vests. Like, argyle sweater vests in the middle of July. I don't know how he doesn't sweat to death in the office, especially because the AC in our building is basically a suggestion. The vents just kind of rattle and blow out lukewarm air. It smells a little bit like old wet paper, too. I brought it up to Steve—the maintenance guy I told you about—and he said the smell was from the "humidity inversion" in the ductwork. Again with the made-up science! I swear he just strings words together to see if I'll believe him. I actually looked up humidity inversion on my phone while he was talking, and it's a real meteorological thing, but it happens in the atmosphere, not in the ceiling of a strip mall accounting firm. I should add that to my spreadsheet. "Steve claims weather phenomenon happening inside office." It's just wild. But yeah, I'm aware I'm doing the things with the receipts and the copier, they just don't make sense to do.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behaviors are intentional rule-breaking/defiant acts versus involuntary stereotyped movements
doctor.question: Do you ever do these behaviors just to break rules or show defiance?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the motivation behind the disorganized behaviors (e.g., if they are done out of defiance), continuing to evaluate the nature of my abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
No, no, it's not about breaking rules at all. I'm actually a really rule-abiding guy. Like I said, I'm a bookkeeper, so rules are kind of my whole life. The IRS has so many rules, and if you mess them up, the fines are crazy. But no, I don't do the things to be defiant. Like I told you when I first came in, I'm only here because I started doing all these things at work and school that just don't make any sense. The lining the receipts up across the floor, the tapping the calculator in sets of nine, standing by the copier with my hands up in the air until someone asks if I'm okay... I don't want to do them, and I'm definitely not trying to get in trouble. 

Getting in trouble at work is the worst, especially with Mr. Henderson. He gets this little vein that pops out on his forehead when he's mad. It's right above his left eyebrow, and it pulses. It's honestly a little distracting. One time, this guy David—he used to work in payroll—he accidentally shredded a whole stack of original W-2s instead of the copies. Mr. Henderson's vein was practically vibrating. David tried to tape them back together, which is just insane. You can't tape a shredded W-2 and send it to the government. They use those cross-cut shredders now, so it was basically confetti. David actually got fired over that. Now he works at a car dealership, I think. Selling used Hondas or something. Hondas are pretty reliable cars, though. My aunt had a Civic that lasted for like, three hundred thousand miles. The only reason it died was because she drove it into a flooded intersection during a storm. The water came right up over the hood. The fire department had to come get her out in a raft. She was so mad about her groceries in the trunk getting ruined. But yeah, no, I'm not trying to be defiant or break rules. I just do these weird things and I don't know why.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the repetitive behaviors are stereotyped, repetitive motor movements typical of stereotypic movement disorder rather than oppositional/defiant behavior.
doctor.question: Do you ever perform the same repetitive movement over and over for several seconds or minutes, like rocking, hand-flapping, or body posturing?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about repetitive movements or body posturing, which are manifestations of disorganized or abnormal motor behavior, aligning with the patient's symptom of standing with hands held up or tapping the calculator.

patient.answer:
I mean, yeah, I guess so. Like I was saying before, that's the whole reason I'm here. I started doing all these weird things at work and school that just don't make any sense at all. Like standing by the copier with my hands held up in the air. I just stand there like that until someone comes by and asks if I'm okay. Or the calculator thing, where I have to tap it in sets of nine. And the receipts, lining them all up across the floor... 

It's so annoying with the receipts because thermal paper fades so fast, you know? If you leave a receipt in your car on a hot day, it just turns completely black. Or if it's in your wallet too long, the ink just disappears and it's a blank piece of paper. I don't understand why they still use thermal printers. It seems like a terrible way to keep permanent records. My dad used to keep all his receipts in this old shoebox under his bed for taxes. It was a Nike box, from these running shoes he bought when he decided he was going to run a marathon. He never actually ran the marathon, though. He trained for like three weeks, pulled a hamstring, and gave up. He said running was bad for your knees anyway. He started swimming instead. He goes to the YMCA every morning at 5 AM. I don't know how anyone wakes up that early on purpose. The pool always smells so strongly of chlorine, it burns my eyes just walking into the building. But yeah, I do those things like the copier and the tapping and the receipts over and over, even though they don't make sense.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the repetitive behaviors are purposeful, socially inappropriate actions done for rule-breaking/defiant reasons versus involuntary stereotyped movements without that intent.
doctor.question: When you do these repetitive behaviors, are they usually done to break rules or show defiance?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the behaviors are done to break rules or show defiance, which relates to oppositional or conduct issues. My symptom profile does not include symptoms of defiance or rule-breaking.

patient.answer:
Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like I was saying a few minutes ago, no, it's not about breaking rules or being defiant at all. I actually hate breaking rules. Even really small ones, like jaywalking. I'll stand at a crosswalk at midnight when there are absolutely zero cars on the road, just waiting for the little white walking guy to light up. 

My friend Tyler used to make fun of me for it all the time. He was always breaking rules, though. Back in high school, he actually got suspended for climbing up onto the roof of the gym just to get a frisbee. Which is so stupid when you think about it, because frisbees are like, what, maybe five dollars? You can literally get them at the dollar store now. They have that whole aisle of cheap plastic summer toys. I bought a squirt gun there once for my little cousin, and it leaked the second I put water in it. Just dripped straight out the bottom of the handle right onto my shoes. I guess you really get what you pay for with that kind of stuff. The plastic is probably terrible for the environment, too. But yeah, to answer your question again, I'm definitely not trying to be defiant or break any rules when I do the weird stuff at work.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the repetitive behaviors are voluntary, intentional rule-breaking/defiant acts versus involuntary motor mannerisms
doctor.question: Do you feel like you choose to do these behaviors, even a little bit?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I have started doing things at work and school that do not make sense, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I am okay.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient has any voluntary control over or chooses to engage in the disorganized and abnormal behaviors previously described, which falls under the symptom of disorganized/abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
No, not at all. That's the whole problem, honestly. Like I said, I only came in here because I started doing all these things at work and school that just don't make any sense, and I don't feel like I'm choosing to do them. The lining the receipts up across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I'm okay... I don't want to do any of it. 

It's actually really embarrassing, especially the copier thing. The copier is right next to the breakroom, so everyone walks past it when they go to get coffee. We just got one of those fancy Keurig machines, too. The ones where you can pick the exact ounce size for your cup. It's supposed to be a perk, but honestly, those little plastic pods are so bad for the earth. I saw a documentary once about how many of those K-cups end up in landfills, and it's millions. They just sit there for centuries because the plastic doesn't break down. It made me want to start composting, but I live in an apartment on the third floor, so I don't really have a yard for a compost bin. My neighbor has a little worm bin on her balcony, though. She says they eat all her vegetable scraps. I think worms are kind of gross, to be honest. They get all slimy when it rains. But yeah, I don't choose to do the weird behaviors. They just happen.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with stereotypic movement disorder: repeated, seemingly purposeless, patterned behaviors (lining up receipts, tapping in sets of nine, standing with hands raised), with onset in multiple settings, partial suppressibility, awareness, and no premonitory urge, anxiety relief, obsessions, or deliberate rule-breaking. Conduct disorder is unlikely because the behaviors are not aggressive, destructive, deceitful, or defiant. OCD is less likely because the patient denies obsessions, compulsive tension, or fear of harm prevention.
